chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:

A man forgot to perform one sajdah from the second [unit] until he stood up, then remembered while he was standing that he had not performed the sajdah. He عليه السلام said: Let him perform the sajdah so long as he has not gone into ruku'. But if he has gone into ruku' and then remembers after his ruku' that he did not perform the sajdah, then let him continue with his salat until he gives salām, then he should perform it, for it is a qada'.

key_terms.رُكُوعِهِ: his ruku', the bowing position in salat
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: a compensatory make-up act performed after its place has passed
key_terms.يُسَلِّمَ: he gives the salām ending the salat

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets one sajdah in salat and remembers after standing or after ruku'?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who forgets a single sajdah in salat. If he remembers before entering ruku', he performs the missed sajdah immediately; if he remembers after ruku', he completes the salat and then makes up the sajdah afterward as qada'.
